book: Agentic AI Engineering: Designing, Evaluating, and Operating Systems That Act

policy.vendor_evidence: May establish documented behavior or a bounded vendor case, never universal superiority
policy.specification_evidence: Version and maturity must be stated; drafts and release candidates are not stable standards
policy.employer_postings: Excluded from the technical source system
policy.fictional_case: FieldOps Relay is synthetic and carries no company outcome claims

sources.title: A practical guide to building agents
sources.supports: Agent definition, suitability, incremental orchestration, tool/guardrail and human-intervention design.
sources.limitations: Provider guidance; examples and recommendations are not comparative proof. Publication date is page-level rather than an editioned standard.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.supports: Workflow/agent distinction, simple composable patterns, model-directed tool use, and complexity tradeoffs.
sources.limitations: Provider-authored synthesis; architecture advice must be tested in the book's task environment.

sources.title: Running agents
sources.supports: Explicit run loop, final-output/tool/handoff branches, maximum turns, resumable run state, sessions and execution configuration.
sources.limitations: Describes one SDK; the book abstracts its semantics and does not prescribe the implementation.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-11-25: Tools
sources.supports: Tool discovery/invocation, input/output schemas, structured results, errors, annotations and security responsibilities.
sources.limitations: Tool annotations are explicitly untrusted unless the server is trusted; transport/protocol conformance does not establish application authorization or safe effect semantics.

sources.title: Writing effective tools for AI agents using AI agents
sources.supports: Tools as agent-facing contracts, namespacing, descriptive schemas, contextual efficiency, prototyping and task-based evaluation.
sources.limitations: The reported process and results are from Anthropic's systems; transfer requires local evaluation.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-11-25: Authorization
sources.supports: OAuth-based authorization, protected-resource metadata, resource indicators, audience validation, PKCE and token-passthrough prohibition.
sources.limitations: Applies to HTTP-based MCP transports; local application delegation and effect approval still require application semantics.

sources.title: RFC 9700: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security
sources.supports: Authorization-code protection, token replay mitigation, audience/privilege restriction, sender constraint and contemporary OAuth threat mitigations.
sources.limitations: OAuth security guidance does not define an agent's business authority or human consent model.

sources.title: RFC 8707: Resource Indicators for OAuth 2.0
sources.supports: Resource-specific token requests and audience restriction.
sources.limitations: Resource indicators narrow token audience; they do not by themselves provide least-privilege scopes or approval binding.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-11-25: Elicitation
sources.supports: Structured and URL-mode user interaction, review/decline/cancel responses, sensitive-data boundaries and verified-user state binding.
sources.limitations: Elicitation is an interaction primitive, not proof that a named human has formal authority for an effect.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
sources.supports: Context as finite model input, iterative curation, compaction, structured notes and subagent context isolation.
sources.limitations: Context-management techniques are provider experience; they do not define authoritative state, retention, privacy or memory governance.

sources.title: Agent Development Kit: State
sources.supports: Session state, scoped keys, persistence through services and state update mechanics.
sources.limitations: Framework semantics are illustrative; application truth, provenance, conflicts and deletion require a local contract.

sources.title: Agent Development Kit: Memory
sources.supports: Cross-session memory services, search and session-to-memory transfer.
sources.limitations: A storage/retrieval API does not establish that retained content is true, authorized, fresh, safe or deletable.

sources.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
sources.supports: A production multi-agent research architecture, delegation, parallel search, evaluation, token/cost tradeoffs and coordination failures.
sources.limitations: Vendor-reported system and metrics for a research task; no independent reproduction and no basis for general multi-agent superiority.

sources.title: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
sources.supports: Ambiguous success, client request identifiers, semantic equivalence, duplicate suppression, late arrivals and auditability.
sources.limitations: Patterns depend on service-side support and careful semantic definition; idempotency does not undo an already-completed effect.

sources.title: REL05-BP03 Control and limit retry calls
sources.supports: Bounded retries, exponential backoff, jitter, retryable-error classification, retry-layer coordination and observability.
sources.limitations: Cloud reliability guidance; exact limits and failure classification remain workload-specific.

sources.title: Temporal documentation: durable execution
sources.supports: One concrete durable-execution model for persisting progress and recovering across process, network and infrastructure failures.
sources.limitations: Vendor implementation, not a universal guarantee; deterministic workflow constraints, activity semantics and deployment compatibility must be respected.
sources.verification: URL and current product description checked 2026-08-16

sources.title: Human-in-the-loop
sources.supports: Tool approval interruption, serializable run state, approval/rejection and resumption.
sources.limitations: SDK mechanism; authorization quality depends on proposal identity, evidence, approver authority, expiry and downstream enforcement.

sources.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
sources.supports: Multi-environment agent evaluation and evidence that environment design materially shapes measured capability.
sources.limitations: Benchmark tasks and historical model results do not establish current production reliability or safe authorization.
sources.verification: Abstract, versions and paper URL checked 2026-08-16

sources.title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
sources.supports: Policy-constrained tool-agent-user task environments, database-state outcomes and repeated-run consistency concerns.
sources.limitations: Synthetic benchmark with specific domains and simulator assumptions; scores cannot be transferred to FieldOps Relay without replication.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.supports: Task construction, graders, transcript inspection, outcome/trajectory evaluation, trial counts and evaluation-driven development.
sources.limitations: Provider guidance; grader validity and statistical sufficiency are use-case dependent.

sources.title: A shared playbook for trustworthy third party evaluations
sources.supports: Harness fidelity, model/tool access, budgets, task validity and reproducibility as parts of evaluation interpretation.
sources.limitations: Provider-authored guidance; not an independent certification framework.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026
sources.supports: Agent-specific threat categories and a structured control-review checklist.
sources.limitations: Risk taxonomy, not a standard, assurance claim or evidence that listed controls are sufficient for a particular system.

sources.title: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency
sources.supports: Risk from excessive functionality, permissions and autonomy; least-privilege and human-approval mitigations.
sources.limitations: High-level risk guidance; it does not specify a complete engineering or formal authorization system.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol security best practices
sources.supports: Token passthrough prohibition, audience validation, session safety, SSRF controls, local-server sandboxing, audit and minimum scopes.
sources.limitations: Protocol-focused guidance; does not replace application threat modeling or domain authority.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions: Generative AI attributes
sources.stability: mixed stability; registry is versioned and evolving
sources.supports: Cross-system names for model, operation, token, tool and agent telemetry fields.
sources.limitations: Semantic conventions do not decide which sensitive content may be collected, retained or exposed; stability must be checked per attribute.
sources.verification: Current registry URL and stability notice checked 2026-08-16

sources.title: Get started with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore observability
sources.supports: One production implementation of OpenTelemetry-compatible agent traces, spans and metrics.
sources.limitations: AWS-specific implementation; product telemetry availability does not prove adequate causal diagnosis or privacy controls.

sources.title: Monitoring distributed systems
sources.supports: Symptom/cause separation, actionable monitoring, latency/error/traffic/saturation signals and distribution-aware operation.
sources.limitations: General SRE guidance predates modern agents; agent run/action/effect semantics are a book synthesis.

sources.title: Canarying releases
sources.supports: Partial time-limited exposure, control/canary comparison, rollout questions, false-positive tradeoffs and automated decision criteria.
sources.limitations: General release engineering; shadow/read-only/approval stages and agent-effect controls are local adaptations.
sources.verification: Official chapter URL and content checked 2026-08-16

sources.title: How we monitor internal coding agents for misalignment
sources.supports: A real deployment's layered monitoring, automated detection, human review and response workflow.
sources.limitations: Provider-selected environment, monitors and reported outcomes; not evidence that monitoring eliminates misalignment or transfers to other domains.

sources.title: Operator System Card
sources.supports: Risk assessment, user confirmation for consequential actions, prompt-injection defenses, monitoring and documented limitations in a browser-acting agent.
sources.limitations: One provider's prerelease system and evaluation; controls and residual risks are product-specific.

sources.title: A2A Protocol Specification v1.0.0
sources.stability: v1.0.0 specification; main branch may advance
sources.supports: Agent discovery, task lifecycle/state, messages, artifacts, streaming, push notifications, extensions and transport bindings.
sources.limitations: Interoperability vocabulary does not establish trust in remote capability claims, local authorization, effect semantics or business completion.
sources.verification: Repository spec and declared v1.0.0 content checked 2026-08-16

sources.title: Developer's guide to AI agent protocols
sources.supports: Different protocol layers and responsibilities, including MCP for tools/context and A2A for agent collaboration.
sources.limitations: Maintainer overview, not the normative specification and not a mandate to adopt multiple protocols.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol 2026-07-28 release candidate
sources.supports: Current direction for tasks, task handles, get/update/cancel operations and authorization hardening.
sources.limitations: Explicitly a release candidate. It may change and cannot be represented as a final stable specification.

sources.title: Inside OpenAI’s in-house data agent
sources.supports: A deployed internal data-agent architecture using context, tools, permissions, evaluation and feedback.
sources.limitations: Internal vendor case; outcomes and architecture are not independently reproduced and include organization-specific data infrastructure.

sources.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
sources.supports: Progress artifacts, structured handoff between context windows, incremental work, clean-state discipline and testable checkpoints.
sources.limitations: Coding-agent harness experience; database effects, distributed leases and formal human authority require additional sources and local design.
sources.verification: Publication listing and article URL checked 2026-08-16

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
sources.stability: published framework; NIST states revision is underway
sources.supports: Govern/map/measure/manage lifecycle, risk ownership, context, measurement, documentation and continuous improvement.
sources.limitations: Voluntary, non-sector-specific framework; it does not prescribe an agent runtime or certify a system. Revision status must be disclosed.
sources.verification: NIST publication and revision notice checked 2026-08-16

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
sources.supports: Generative-AI risk identification, measurement, documentation, incident disclosure and lifecycle management considerations.
sources.limitations: Cross-sector profile, not agent-specific assurance or sector authorization; implementation remains contextual.

sources.title: Accelerating the Adoption of Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization
sources.stability: concept paper; not final standard or guidance
sources.supports: Current identity/authorization problem framing for software and AI agents, delegation, credentials and accountability.
sources.limitations: Concept paper only. It must never be described as a standard, normative control set or completed reference architecture.
sources.verification: Official PDF, title and status checked 2026-08-16

sources.title: A2A Protocol normative protobuf
sources.supports: Normative task, message, artifact, status and service definitions behind A2A bindings.
sources.limitations: Main-branch source must be pinned to a tag/commit before publication; schema conformance is not semantic compatibility.

sources.title: Tracing
sources.supports: Run, agent, model, function, guardrail and handoff spans plus custom trace processors and sensitive-data configuration.
sources.limitations: SDK telemetry model; default tracing and redaction settings must be verified, and traces alone do not prove causation or correctness.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-11-25: Tasks
sources.stability: experimental in 2025-11-25; supersession work visible in 2026-07-28 RC
sources.supports: Protocol-level representation of long-running requests, status, result retrieval and cancellation.
sources.limitations: Experimental edition. Application durability, ownership, effect recovery and approval semantics remain outside the protocol.
sources.verification: Version, experimental notice and current RC relationship checked 2026-08-16

sources.title: Agent Development Kit: Multi-agent systems
sources.supports: One framework's hierarchy, delegation and workflow-agent composition patterns.
sources.limitations: Framework mechanics are examples, not evidence that multiple agents improve a task or define complete handoff semantics.

sources.title: ChatGPT agent system card: user confirmations
sources.supports: Confirmation-before-action and active supervision patterns, monitor layers and provider-run evaluation evidence.
sources.limitations: Product-specific controls and provider-run tests; confirmation can reduce but not eliminate mistaken or manipulated action.
sources.verification: URL and current page content checked 2026-08-16

sources.title: RFC 9728: OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata
sources.supports: Protected-resource metadata discovery and authorization-server relationship used by current MCP authorization.
sources.limitations: Metadata discovery must be implemented securely and does not prove resource trust or authorize a business effect.
